export type GatewayExamItem = {
  prompt: string;
  answer: string;
  acceptable?: readonly string[];
};

export type GatewayEnhancement = {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  liveLabel: string;
  liveValue: (t: number) => string;
  misconception: { wrong: string; correction: string };
  unlocks: { ids: readonly number[]; sentence: string; nextHref: string; nextLabel: string };
  exams: readonly [GatewayExamItem, GatewayExamItem, GatewayExamItem];
};

function g(
  id: number,
  title: string,
  liveLabel: string,
  liveValue: (t: number) => string,
  wrong: string,
  correction: string,
  unlockIds: readonly number[],
  sentence: string,
  nextHref: string,
  nextLabel: string,
  exams: readonly [GatewayExamItem, GatewayExamItem, GatewayExamItem],
): GatewayEnhancement {
  return {
    id,
    title,
    liveLabel,
    liveValue,
    misconception: { wrong, correction },
    unlocks: { ids: unlockIds, sentence, nextHref, nextLabel },
    exams,
  };
}

const exam = (prompt: string, answer: string, ...acceptable: string[]): GatewayExamItem => ({
  prompt,
  answer,
  acceptable,
});

export const gatewayEnhancementIds = [
  1, 2, 39, 40, 60, 61, 76, 77, 78, 92, 94, 96, 99, 107, 111, 112, 115, 130, 133, 134, 167, 214, 220,
  258, 259, 277, 284, 439, 470, 508, 2001, 2006, 2011, 2016, 2024, 10001, 10017, 10028, 10033, 10057,
  10066, 10083, 10092, 10124, 10134, 10165, 10180, 10200, 10210, 10214,
] as const;

export const gatewayEnhancements: Record<number, GatewayEnhancement> = {
  1: g(1, "Basic Calculator", "BODMAS next value", (t) => String([20, 5, 15][Math.round(t * 2)]),
    "Working left to right and ignoring brackets.",
    "Do brackets first: (12+8)=20, then 20÷4=5.",
    [2], "Unlocks fraction arithmetic on the same workspace.",
    "/lessons/core-workspaces/2-fraction-calculator", "Fraction Calculator",
    [exam("Evaluate (12+8)÷4.", "5"), exam("What is done first in 3+(2×5)?", "2×5", "2*5", "multiplication"), exam("Is 8-3+1 equal to 4?", "no")]),
  2: g(2, "Fraction Calculator", "LCD fourths", (t) => `${2 + Math.round(t * 3)}/4`,
    "Adding numerators and denominators separately, 1/2+3/4=4/6.",
    "Rewrite 1/2 as 2/4, then add 2/4+3/4=5/4.",
    [76, 77, 78], "Unlocks equivalent fractions, comparison, and mixed operations.",
    "/lessons/numbers-and-arithmetic/76-equivalent-fractions", "Equivalent Fractions",
    [exam("Compute 1/2 + 3/4.", "5/4", "1 1/4"), exam("Compute 2/3 − 1/6.", "1/2"), exam("Does 1/2 + 1/3 equal 2/5?", "no")]),
  39: g(39, "Cartesian Graphing", "plotted point", (t) => `(${Math.round(-2 + t * 6)}, ${Math.round(-1 + t * 4)})`,
    "Swapping the x- and y-coordinates when plotting.",
    "x is horizontal, y is vertical. Plot (3,4) three right and four up.",
    [40], "Unlocks function plotting on the same axes.",
    "/lessons/graphs-and-functions/40-function-plotter", "Function Plotter",
    [exam("What is the x-coordinate of (3,4)?", "3"), exam("In which quadrant is (−2,5)?", "2", "II", "second"), exam("Does (0,4) lie on the x-axis?", "no")]),
  40: g(40, "Function Plotter", "y = 2x+1", (t) => String(2 * Math.round(-2 + t * 6) + 1),
    "Reading a point on the curve as if x and y were independent.",
    "Each plotted point must satisfy y=f(x). At x=3, y=7 on y=2x+1.",
    [167], "Unlocks the coordinate plane used by geometry and vectors.",
    "/lessons/geometry/167-cartesian-plane", "Cartesian Plane",
    [exam("If y=2x+1 and x=3, what is y?", "7"), exam("Which point is on y=x²: (2,4) or (2,3)?", "(2,4)", "2,4"), exam("Is a vertical line x=2 a function of x?", "no")]),
  60: g(60, "Rational Numbers", "decimal form", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "3/4 = 0.75" : "1/3 = 0.333…"),
    "Calling every non-terminating decimal irrational.",
    "1/3 = 0.333… is rational because it repeats. Irrational decimals never repeat.",
    [61], "Unlocks irrationals, surds, and the completed real line.",
    "/lessons/numbers-and-arithmetic/61-irrational-numbers", "Irrational Numbers",
    [exam("Write 3/4 as a decimal.", "0.75"), exam("Is 0.333… rational?", "yes"), exam("Is √2 equal to 22/7?", "no")]),
  61: g(61, "Irrational Numbers", "√2 versus 22/7", (t) => (1.414 + t * 0.0002).toFixed(4),
    "Treating a long decimal approximation as the exact irrational.",
    "22/7 and 1.414 are rationals near √2. √2 itself does not terminate or repeat.",
    [92], "Unlocks algebra tiles once number types are settled.",
    "/lessons/algebra/92-algebra-tiles", "Algebra Tiles",
    [exam("Is √2 rational?", "no"), exam("Is 22/7 exactly π?", "no"), exam("Does 1.414 equal √2?", "no")]),
  76: g(76, "Equivalent Fractions", "same share", (t) => `${1 + Math.round(t * 3)}/${2 + Math.round(t * 6)}`,
    "Changing only the numerator and calling the fraction equivalent.",
    "Multiply or divide numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number.",
    [77], "Unlocks fair comparison of unlike fractions.",
    "/lessons/numbers-and-arithmetic/77-comparing-fractions", "Comparing Fractions",
    [exam("Write a fraction equivalent to 2/3 with denominator 12.", "8/12"), exam("Are 2/4 and 1/2 equivalent?", "yes"), exam("Does multiplying only the numerator by 2 keep the value?", "no")]),
  77: g(77, "Comparing Fractions", "cross product", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "3/4 > 2/3" : "9 > 8"),
    "Comparing numerators only, or denominators only.",
    "Cross-multiply: 3×3=9 and 2×4=8, so 3/4 > 2/3.",
    [78], "Unlocks adding and subtracting after a common denominator.",
    "/lessons/numbers-and-arithmetic/78-fraction-operations", "Fraction Operations",
    [exam("Which is greater: 3/4 or 2/3?", "3/4"), exam("Compare 5/6 and 4/5 using cross products. First product 5×5?", "25"), exam("Is 2/5 greater than 3/7?", "no")]),
  78: g(78, "Fraction Operations", "1/2 + 1/3", (t) => (t < 0.34 ? "3/6" : t < 0.67 ? "2/6" : "5/6"),
    "Using different operations with the same unreduced pair.",
    "Convert to sixths first: 3/6+2/6=5/6. Multiplication is 1/6, not 5/6.",
    [60], "Unlocks the rational-number classification of these answers.",
    "/lessons/numbers-and-arithmetic/60-rational-numbers", "Rational Numbers",
    [exam("Compute 1/2 + 1/3.", "5/6"), exam("Compute 1/2 × 1/3.", "1/6"), exam("Is 1/2 ÷ 1/4 equal to 1/8?", "no")]),
  92: g(92, "Algebra Tiles", "zero pairs", (t) => String(Math.round(t * 4)),
    "Removing a tile without its opposite zero pair.",
    "A +1 tile and a −1 tile cancel. The remaining tiles are the simplified expression.",
    [94], "Unlocks substitution into the simplified expression.",
    "/lessons/algebra/94-substitution", "Substitution",
    [exam("How many zero pairs cancel +3 and −3?", "3"), exam("Simplify 2x + 3 − 3.", "2x"), exam("Can you cancel x in (x+2)/x without a common factor?", "no")]),
  94: g(94, "Substitution", "3x+5 at x", (t) => String(3 * Math.round(-2 + t * 6) + 5),
    "Replacing only the first x and leaving later x unchanged.",
    "Every x becomes the same value. If x=−2, 3x+5=−1.",
    [96], "Unlocks expanding products after substitution checks.",
    "/lessons/algebra/96-double-brackets", "Double Brackets",
    [exam("Evaluate 3x+5 when x=−2.", "-1"), exam("Evaluate x² when x=4.", "16"), exam("If x=2, is 2x+x equal to 2(2)+2?", "yes")]),
  96: g(96, "Double Brackets", "(x+2)(x+3)", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "x²+5x+6" : "2×3=6"),
    "Adding the insides and outsides only, forgetting the four products.",
    "Four products: x² + 3x + 2x + 6 = x²+5x+6.",
    [99], "Unlocks index laws used when expanding powers.",
    "/lessons/algebra/99-indices", "Indices",
    [exam("Expand (x+2)(x+3).", "x^2+5x+6", "x²+5x+6"), exam("What is the constant term of (x+4)(x+5)?", "20"), exam("Is (x+2)² equal to x²+4?", "no")]),
  99: g(99, "Indices", "2^n", (t) => String(2 ** (1 + Math.round(t * 4))),
    "Adding exponents when the bases are different, or multiplying exponents for a product.",
    "Same base: a^m · a^n = a^{m+n}. 2^3 · 2^2 = 2^5 = 32.",
    [107], "Unlocks one-step equations that use powers as coefficients.",
    "/lessons/algebra/107-one-step-equations", "One-Step Equations",
    [exam("Compute 2^3 · 2^2.", "32"), exam("What is 5^0?", "1"), exam("Is 2^3 · 3^2 equal to 6^5?", "no")]),
  107: g(107, "One-Step Equations", "2x = 10", (t) => String(5 * (0.4 + t)),
    "Subtracting 2 from 2x=10 instead of dividing by 2.",
    "The inverse of ×2 is ÷2. 2x=10 ⇒ x=5.",
    [111], "Unlocks multi-step linear equations.",
    "/lessons/algebra/111-linear-equations", "Linear Equations",
    [exam("Solve 2x=10.", "5"), exam("Solve x+7=12.", "5"), exam("Is the inverse of ×3 the operation −3?", "no")]),
  111: g(111, "Linear Equations", "2x+3", (t) => String(2 * Math.round(1 + t * 5) + 3),
    "Moving a term across the equals sign without changing its sign.",
    "2x+3=11 ⇒ 2x=8 ⇒ x=4. Subtract 3 from both sides.",
    [112], "Unlocks two-equation systems.",
    "/lessons/algebra/112-simultaneous-linear-equations", "Simultaneous Linear Equations",
    [exam("Solve 2x+3=11.", "4"), exam("If 3x−6=9, what is x?", "5"), exam("Does adding 3 to only one side keep an equation true?", "no")]),
  112: g(112, "Simultaneous Linear Equations", "intersection", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "(2, 3)" : "x=2, y=3"),
    "Solving one equation and ignoring the second.",
    "The solution is the intersection. x+y=5 and x−y=1 give (2,3).",
    [115], "Unlocks higher-degree polynomial roots.",
    "/lessons/algebra/115-polynomial-equations", "Polynomial Equations",
    [exam("Solve x+y=5 and x−y=1. What is x?", "2"), exam("What is y in that system?", "3"), exam("If two lines have the same slope and different intercepts, do they intersect?", "no")]),
  115: g(115, "Polynomial Equations", "roots of (x-1)(x-2)", (t) => String(1 + Math.round(t)),
    "Forgetting a factor and reporting only one root.",
    "(x−1)(x−2)=0 has roots 1 and 2. A product is zero when a factor is zero.",
    [130], "Unlocks domain and range of the related polynomial graph.",
    "/lessons/graphs-and-functions/130-domain-and-range", "Domain and Range",
    [exam("Roots of (x-1)(x-2)=0?", "1 and 2", "1,2"), exam("How many real roots can a quadratic have?", "0, 1, or 2", "0 1 or 2"), exam("If x=0, is x(x-3)=0 true?", "yes")]),
  130: g(130, "Domain and Range", "√(x+d) start", (t) => `x ≥ ${(-2 + Math.round(t * 4)).toString()}`,
    "Including x-values that make the inside of a square root negative.",
    "For y=√(x−d), the domain is x≥d. A hole is a missing point, not a new endpoint.",
    [133], "Unlocks linear functions on a restricted or full domain.",
    "/lessons/graphs-and-functions/133-linear-functions", "Linear Functions",
    [exam("Domain of y=√(x-2)?", "x≥2", "x >= 2"), exam("Range of y=√x for real x?", "y≥0", "y >= 0"), exam("Is x=−4 in the domain of y=√x?", "no")]),
  133: g(133, "Linear Functions", "slope triangle", (t) => `m=${(0.5 + t * 1.5).toFixed(1)}`,
    "Reading rise/run with run=0, or calling a vertical line a function.",
    "Slope is Δy/Δx. A vertical line has undefined slope and is not y=f(x).",
    [134], "Unlocks quadratic graphs after the straight-line case.",
    "/lessons/graphs-and-functions/134-quadratic-functions", "Quadratic Functions",
    [exam("Slope of the line through (0,1) and (2,7)?", "3"), exam("y-intercept of y=3x-4?", "-4"), exam("Is x=2 a linear function of x?", "no")]),
  134: g(134, "Quadratic Functions", "vertex of x²-4x+3", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "(2, -1)" : "roots 1 and 3"),
    "Treating the vertex x-coordinate as −b instead of −b/(2a).",
    "For y=x²−4x+3, vertex is (2,−1) and roots are 1 and 3.",
    [258], "Unlocks the unit circle after parabolas.",
    "/lessons/trigonometry/258-unit-circle", "Unit Circle",
    [exam("Vertex of y=x²-4x+3?", "(2,-1)", "(2, −1)"), exam("Roots of x²-4x+3=0?", "1 and 3", "1,3"), exam("If a>0, does the parabola open downward?", "no")]),
  167: g(167, "Cartesian Plane", "quadrant", (t) => ["I", "II", "III", "IV"][Math.round(t * 3)],
    "Numbering quadrants clockwise, or putting signs on the wrong axis.",
    "I (+,+), II (−,+), III (−,−), IV (+,−). Signs are (x, y).",
    [214], "Unlocks triangle construction on the plane.",
    "/lessons/geometry/214-triangle-constructor", "Triangle Constructor",
    [exam("Quadrant of (−3, 2)?", "2", "II", "second"), exam("What are the signs in quadrant III?", "(-,-)", "(−,−)"), exam("Does (4,0) lie in a quadrant?", "no")]),
  214: g(214, "Triangle Constructor", "SSS check", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "3,4,5 yes" : "2,3,6 no"),
    "Drawing three sides without checking the triangle inequality.",
    "Sides a,b,c form a triangle only if a+b>c for every pairing. 2+3=5≯6.",
    [220], "Unlocks the unique circle through three non-collinear points.",
    "/lessons/geometry/220-circle-through-three-points", "Circle Through Three Points",
    [exam("Can 3,4,5 form a triangle?", "yes"), exam("Can 2,3,6 form a triangle?", "no"), exam("SSS uses how many sides?", "3")]),
  220: g(220, "Circle Through Three Points", "circumradius idea", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "unique circle" : "collinear: none"),
    "Claiming three collinear points still determine a finite circle.",
    "Three non-collinear points determine one circle. Collinear points do not.",
    [258], "Unlocks the unit circle as a special labelled case.",
    "/lessons/trigonometry/258-unit-circle", "Unit Circle",
    [exam("How many circles pass through 3 non-collinear points?", "1"), exam("Do 3 collinear points determine a finite circle?", "no"), exam("The centre is the intersection of what?", "perpendicular bisectors")]),
  258: g(258, "Unit Circle", "θ coordinates", (t) => {
    const deg = Math.round(t * 90);
    const rad = (deg * Math.PI) / 180;
    return `${deg}° → (${Math.cos(rad).toFixed(2)}, ${Math.sin(rad).toFixed(2)})`;
  },
    "Reading sine as the x-coordinate on the unit circle.",
    "On the unit circle, x=cos θ and y=sin θ. At 90°, (0,1).",
    [259], "Unlocks right-triangle ratios as the first-quadrant case.",
    "/lessons/trigonometry/259-right-triangle-ratios", "Right-Triangle Ratios",
    [exam("cos 0°?", "1"), exam("sin 90°?", "1"), exam("Is sin 30° equal to the x-coordinate of that point?", "no")]),
  259: g(259, "Right-Triangle Ratios", "tan θ", (t) => {
    const deg = 15 + Math.round(t * 60);
    return `tan ${deg}° ≈ ${Math.tan((deg * Math.PI) / 180).toFixed(2)}`;
  },
    "Swapping opposite and adjacent after the triangle is rotated.",
    "Opposite faces the marked angle. tan θ = opposite/adjacent.",
    [277], "Unlocks informal limits of these ratios as θ shrinks.",
    "/lessons/calculus/277-informal-limits", "Informal Limits",
    [exam("sin 30°?", "1/2", "0.5"), exam("cos 60°?", "1/2", "0.5"), exam("Is tan θ opposite/hypotenuse?", "no")]),
  277: g(277, "Informal Limits", "left vs right", (t) => (t < 0.5 ? "left → 2" : "right → 2"),
    "Saying the limit fails because f(a) is missing.",
    "A hole can still have a limit if both sides agree. Left and right must match.",
    [284], "Unlocks average rate of change as a secant limit.",
    "/lessons/calculus/284-average-rate-of-change", "Average Rate of Change",
    [exam("If left=2 and right=2, does the two-sided limit exist?", "yes"), exam("If left=2 and right=3, does it exist?", "no"), exam("Does a hole automatically destroy the limit?", "no")]),
  284: g(284, "Average Rate of Change", "secant Δy/Δx", (t) => {
    const h = 2 - t * 1.5;
    return ((4 + 2 * h) / 1).toFixed(1);
  },
    "Calling the secant slope the derivative on a wide interval.",
    "Average rate uses a secant. The derivative is the limit as the interval shrinks.",
    [439], "Unlocks symbolic derivatives of the same functions.",
    "/lessons/symbolic-mathematics/439-derivatives", "Derivatives",
    [exam("Average rate of x² from 1 to 3?", "4"), exam("Δx from 2 to 5?", "3"), exam("Is average rate the same as f'(x) on a long interval?", "no")]),
  439: g(439, "Derivatives", "d/dx x²", (t) => String(2 * Math.round(-2 + t * 6)),
    "Differentiating x² as 2x² or as x.",
    "Power rule: d/dx x² = 2x. At x=3 the slope is 6.",
    [470], "Unlocks statistics after the calculus spine.",
    "/lessons/data-and-probability/470-mean", "Mean",
    [exam("d/dx of x² at x=3?", "6"), exam("d/dx of 5x?", "5"), exam("Is the derivative of a constant 1?", "no")]),
  470: g(470, "Mean", "balance point", (t) => ((4 + t * 4) ).toFixed(2),
    "Treating the mean as the middle value, or as a data value that must appear.",
    "Mean is total÷count. It is a balance point and need not be one of the data values.",
    [508], "Unlocks conditional probability after a centre is understood.",
    "/lessons/data-and-probability/508-conditional-probability", "Conditional Probability",
    [exam("Mean of 2,4,6,8?", "5"), exam("Mean of 3,3,3,3?", "3"), exam("Must the mean be one of the data values?", "no")]),
  508: g(508, "Conditional Probability", "P(A|B)", (t) => ((0.2 + t * 0.3) ).toFixed(2),
    "Replacing P(A|B) with P(A and B), or swapping A and B.",
    "P(A|B)=P(A and B)/P(B). The condition B is the new sample space.",
    [10210], "Unlocks the Class 12 conditional-probability exam path.",
    "/lessons/school/class-12/class-12-probability-conditional-probability", "School Conditional Probability",
    [exam("If P(A and B)=0.2 and P(B)=0.5, what is P(A|B)?", "0.4", "2/5"), exam("Is P(A|B) the same as P(B|A) in general?", "no"), exam("Can a conditional probability exceed 1?", "no")]),
  2001: g(2001, "Partial Quotients", "a0 for x", (t) => String(Math.floor(1 + t * 3)),
    "Reading decimal digits as continued-fraction quotients.",
    "Each quotient is a floor of a reciprocal remainder, not a decimal digit.",
    [2002, 2006], "Unlocks convergents and then famous-problem experiments.",
    "/lessons/advanced-concepts/2002-convergents", "Convergents",
    [exam("First partial quotient of 7/5?", "1"), exam("Reciprocal of remainder 2/5?", "5/2"), exam("Are decimal digits the partial quotients?", "no")]),
  2006: g(2006, "Collatz Conjecture", "next hailstone", (t) => {
    const n = 6 + Math.round(t * 9);
    return String(n % 2 === 0 ? n / 2 : 3 * n + 1);
  },
    "Treating a long computed orbit as a proof for every n.",
    "One hailstone path is evidence. The conjecture claims every positive integer reaches 1.",
    [2011], "Unlocks statistical inference after experiment-versus-proof.",
    "/lessons/advanced-concepts/2011-confidence-intervals", "Confidence Intervals",
    [exam("Next Collatz term after 6?", "3"), exam("Next term after 5?", "16"), exam("Does a path to 1 prove the conjecture?", "no")]),
  2011: g(2011, "Confidence Intervals", "x̄ ± ME", (t) => {
    const me = 1 + Math.round(t * 3);
    return `${10} ± ${me}`;
  },
    "Saying a 95% CI contains the sample mean only 95% of the time.",
    "A symmetric CI is built around the sample mean. 95% refers to the method across samples.",
    [2016], "Unlocks slope fields after a numeric interval model.",
    "/lessons/advanced-concepts/2016-slope-fields", "Slope Fields",
    [exam("If x̄=10 and ME=2, upper bound?", "12"), exam("Does a symmetric CI contain x̄ by construction?", "yes"), exam("Does one interval prove μ is inside it?", "no")]),
  2016: g(2016, "Slope Fields", "slope at x", (t) => String((-2 + t * 6).toFixed(1)),
    "Reading the field as the unique solution without an initial point.",
    "The field is a direction map. An IVP picks one curve through a point.",
    [2024], "Unlocks special functions that solve notable DEs.",
    "/lessons/advanced-concepts/2024-zeta-function", "Zeta Function",
    [exam("If dy/dx=x and x=2, what slope is drawn?", "2"), exam("Does a slope field alone give a unique solution?", "no"), exam("Euler step: y1=y0+h f. If y0=1, h=1, f=2, y1?", "3")]),
  2024: g(2024, "Zeta Function", "partial sum of 1/n^2", (t) => (1 + t * 0.64).toFixed(2),
    "Treating ζ(-1)=−1/12 as ordinary summation of 1+2+3+…",
    "ζ(2)=π²/6 comes from a convergent series. Negative arguments use analytic continuation.",
    [], "This is the last advanced gateway in the set. Return to the advanced list.",
    "/lessons/advanced-concepts", "Advanced lessons",
    [exam("Is ζ(2) greater than 1?", "yes"), exam("Does the series for ζ(2) converge?", "yes"), exam("Does ζ(-1)=-1/12 mean 1+2+3+… converges ordinarily?", "no")]),
  10001: g(10001, "Place Value Explorer", "hundreds value", (t) => String(100 * (1 + Math.round(t * 8))),
    "Reading a digit as ones regardless of place.",
    "In 4791 the 7 is 700, not 7. Place decides value.",
    [10017], "Unlocks ratio tables that still depend on place.",
    "/lessons/school/class-7/class-7-numbers-and-arithmetic-ratio-tables", "Ratio Tables",
    [exam("Value of hundreds digit in 4791?", "700"), exam("How many tens in 40?", "4"), exam("Does the digit 4 always mean four ones?", "no")]),
  10017: g(10017, "Ratio Tables", "scale factor", (t) => `${2 * (1 + Math.round(t * 4))}:${3 * (1 + Math.round(t * 4))}`,
    "Adding the same number to both parts instead of multiplying.",
    "Equivalent ratios use a common multiplier. 2:3 → 8:12 by ×4.",

export function normalizeGatewayAnswer(value: string) {
  return value.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, "").replace(/−/g, "-");
}

export function gatewayAnswerMatches(item: GatewayExamItem, value: string) {
  const actual = normalizeGatewayAnswer(value);
  const allowed = [item.answer, ...(item.acceptable ?? [])].map(normalizeGatewayAnswer);
  return allowed.includes(actual);
}
